\section[la relación]{la relación — the relationship}

\label{lesson:ES-C745-relacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the suitor, then the Spanish for closeness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la relación}
\textbf{la relación} — \textquotedblleft{}the relationship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tenemos una buena relación.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We have a good relationship.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar en una relación} — to be in a relationship.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{relación} comes from Latin \emph{relātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a carrying back, a report\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{referre}, built on \emph{ferre} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la relación}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la relación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la relación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the suitor, then the Spanish for closeness, then say \emph{la relación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la relación mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The relationship\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la ruptura]{la ruptura — the break-up}

\label{lesson:ES-C745-ruptura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for closeness, then the Spanish for the relationship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la ruptura}
\textbf{la ruptura} — \textquotedblleft{}the break-up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Después de la ruptura, se fue a vivir sola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the break-up, she went to live alone.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ruptura} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ruptūra} \textquotedblleft{}a breaking\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{rumpere} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, the source of \emph{romper}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[infiel]{infiel — unfaithful}

\label{lesson:ES-C745-infiel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the relationship, then the Spanish for the break-up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: infiel}
\textbf{infiel} — \textquotedblleft{}unfaithful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Descubrió que su novio le era infiel.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She found out her boyfriend was unfaithful.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ser infiel a alguien}. \emph{La infidelidad} — infidelity.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{infiel} comes from Latin \emph{īnfidēlis} \textquotedblleft{}unfaithful\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{fidēlis} \textquotedblleft{}faithful\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{fidēs} \textquotedblleft{}faith\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[traicionar]{traicionar — to betray}

\label{lesson:ES-C745-traicionar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the break-up, then the Spanish for unfaithful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: traicionar}
\textbf{traicionar} — \textquotedblleft{}to betray\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me traicionó mi mejor amigo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{traicionar} is built on \emph{traición}, usually traced to Latin \emph{trāditiō} \textquotedblleft{}a handing over\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{trādere} \textquotedblleft{}to hand over\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[la traición]{la traición — betrayal, treason}

\label{lesson:ES-C745-traicion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for unfaithful, then the Spanish for to betray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la traición}
\textbf{la traición} — \textquotedblleft{}betrayal, treason\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fue una traición imperdonable.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was an unforgivable betrayal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{traición} is usually traced to Latin \emph{trāditiō}, \emph{trāditiōnem} \textquotedblleft{}a handing over\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{trādere} \textquotedblleft{}to hand over\textquotedblright{}; English \emph{treason} is the same word through French.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
